A_target.statement:
Let $R$ be a [[Definition:Ring with Unity|ring with unity]].
An $R$-[[Definition:Module|module]] is an [[Definition:Abelian Group|abelian group]] $\struct {M, +}$ with an action $R \times M \to M$ satisfying [[Definition:Distributive Operation|distributivity]], [[Definition:Associative Operation|associativity]] and unitality.

B_source.statement: A [[Definition:Vector Space|vector space]] over a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]] $F$ is an abelian group with an action of $F$ satisfying the same axioms.

substitutions.the notion of dimension: the notion of rank, which may fail to be well defined

derived.linear independence and spanning: the same definitions, but bases need not exist

object_map.reformulation: Vector space proofs must be audited for hidden uses of division before they are reused, since the axioms alone do not flag where invertibility was assumed.

validity_conditions: the ring must have an identity for unitality to be stated, or the module is called non-unital
results depending on division by nonzero scalars do not transfer, so every vector space theorem must be re-examined rather than assumed
the existence of a basis fails in general, so dimension arguments must be replaced by rank or by finiteness hypotheses
proof_plan: Take the [[Definition:Vector Space Axioms|vector space axioms]] verbatim and replace the field $F$ by a ring $R$.
[[Definition:Submodule|Submodules]], [[Definition:Quotient Module|quotients]] and the [[First Isomorphism Theorem for Modules|isomorphism theorems]] use only the axioms, and survive.
Results using invertibility of scalars fail, such as existence of a [[Definition:Basis of Module|basis]] and the [[Rank-Nullity Theorem]].
Over $\Z$, the module $\Z / 2 \Z$ has no basis, since $2 x = 0$ for all $x$.

Restrict to [[Definition:Free Module|free]] or [[Definition:Projective Module|projective]] modules to recover these conclusions when needed.
{{qed}}
